newsitem.title: UK: French demand lifts NWE gas oil cargoes, barges dull.
newsitem.headline: French demand lifts NWE gas oil cargoes, barges dull.

text.p: French buying supported prompt NWE gas oil cargo premiums on Tuesday but barges were dull on ice-related delivery problems and indifferent demand, traders said.
Benchmark February IPE gas oil futures ended 75 cents adrift at $203.25 a tonne, easing from earlier highs on weaker NYMEX crude futures.
A European major bought a 20,000 tonne cargo of low sulphur diesel at Feb +$21 prompt cif Le Havre, around $3 above levels at the week's start, and now wants another prompt 20,000 tonner.
Traders suspected the demand was triggered by a need to meet French minimum strategic stock reqirements.
Russian heating oil reflected the long Russian market by trading easier at Feb +$4 for Feb 1-10 cif NWE, although prompt was reportedly done unchanged at Feb +$7 cif NWE.

Bulls pointed to forecasts of below normal weather in the next 6-10 days, arguing prompt French heat was still close to the +$14 paid on Tuesday. Bu bears note French heat traded $1 easier for Feb 1-10 delivery at Feb IPE +$3.50 cif Le Havre.
Barges were quiet, with heating oil pressured by delivery problems, lacklustre demand and dollar firmness. Heating oil traded at Feb IPE +$6/5.75 fob Rotterdam.
